tools.name: search_services
tools.description: Finds services in the catalog of 9,700+ status pages by name, with their status now. Use it to find a service’s slug.

tools.name: get_service
tools.description: One service’s status from its official status page: what’s wrong, the components with a problem, 90 days of history and recent incidents.

tools.name: list_outages
tools.description: Services reporting a problem right now, the newest first: the 25 best-known, unless all is true or a limit is given.

tools.name: list_dashboards
tools.description: The account’s dashboards (the ones this connection can see), with how many services and URL monitors each has and its worst status now.

tools.name: get_stack_status
tools.description: What’s going on now on a dashboard: a summary, then every service and URL monitor with a problem, with when the problem began and when its current status did. A URL monitor that’s down lists what started around then. Without a dashboard, every dashboard.

tools.name: get_incident_history
tools.description: Incidents on a dashboard in a window: the ones that started in it (with what else started at the same time) and the ones already going on. As far back as the plan’s history goes.

tools.name: get_monitor
tools.description: One of the account’s URL monitors: its status, its uptime over the last 30 days (or since it started) with the failed checks apart, response times, its certificate and its latest checks.

tools.name: get_reliability
tools.description: How reliable a dashboard’s services and URL monitors were over 7, 30 or 90 days: the least reliable first, with the share of time without a reported problem (minor issues count, so one long minor issue makes it low), time in each severity, incidents and recovery, and what tends to break together.

tools.name: create_dashboard
tools.description: Makes a dashboard with a name and, optionally, services by slug (search_services finds them), within the plan’s dashboards and services. Answers with its address.

tools.name: rename_dashboard
tools.description: Renames a dashboard. Its status page shares the name.

tools.name: add_services
tools.description: Adds services to a dashboard by slug (search_services finds them), within the plan’s limit.

tools.name: remove_services
tools.description: Takes services off a dashboard. Their history stays; adding one back shows it again.

tools.name: add_monitor
tools.description: Watches a website or API endpoint on a dashboard: checks the address once first, and refuses what the app refuses (private addresses, other ports, past the plan). Without a name, the page’s title names it. Headers and request bodies stay in the app.

tools.name: check_monitor
tools.description: Checks one of the account’s URL monitors now, as Check now does in the app, and says what it got.

tools.name: pause_monitor
tools.description: Pauses a URL monitor, e.g. during a deploy: an open incident ends, and no alerts go out until it’s resumed.

tools.name: resume_monitor
tools.description: Resumes a paused URL monitor: it’s checked at once and starts fresh.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_dashboards, get_stack_status, get_monitor, get_reliability, check_monitor, pause_monitor · Private data: add_monitor · Public sink: get_reliability · Destructive: remove_services.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_dashboards, get_stack_status, get_monitor, get_reliability, check_monitor, pause_monitor · Private data: add_monitor · Public sink: get_reliability · Destructive: remove_services

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
